outlineSections.heading: I. Fundamental Accounting Principles, Concepts, Assumptions and Conventions
points: Nature and scope of accounting, accrual/matching concept, consistency of presentation and comparability.
True and fair view, neutrality, materiality, prudence, completeness, understandability and usefulness.
Going concern and substance over form.

outlineSections.heading: II. Accounting Cycle/Process and Financial Statements
points: Transactions/events, general journal, general ledger, trial balance (unadjusted), adjusting entries and adjusted trial balance, worksheet.
Financial statements: income statement, statement of financial position (balance sheet), statement of cash flows, statement of changes in equity.
Framework as specified by IASB through IFRSs/IASs and by SECP through Companies Ordinance 1984.
Closing and reversing entries.

outlineSections.heading: III. Attributes and Significance of Accounting Information
points: Attributes of accounting information.
Information/reporting requirements of external stakeholders: investors/shareholders, creditors, suppliers, lenders/financiers, government agencies.
Information/reporting requirements of internal stakeholders: board of directors, partners, managers, employees.

outlineSections.heading: IV. Accounting for Common Legal Forms of a Business
points: Accounting principles and financial statements of sole proprietorships, partnerships and joint stock companies including banking companies.
Excluding advanced topics like amalgamation, capital reduction and consolidation.

outlineSections.heading: V. Accounting for Associations Not-for-profit, and for Public Sector
points: Accounting principles and financial statements of not-for-profit associations.
Accounting principles and financial statements of public sector entities as per IPSAS and practices followed in the country.

outlineSections.heading: VI. Accounting for Non-current Tangible Assets
points: Concepts concerning non-current assets: cost, depreciable amount, depreciation, fair value, property/plant/equipment, residual value, useful life.
Depreciation methods: straight-line, reducing balance, number of units produced, and basic know-how of other industry methods.

outlineSections.heading: VII. Fundamental and Technical Analysis of Organizations
points: Financial statement analysis through horizontal (measuring change) and vertical (ratio) analysis.
Liquidity, activity, debt, profitability and market ratios.
Technical and industry analysis.

outlineSections.heading: VIII. Fundamental Cost Accounting Principles and Concepts
points: Nature and scope of cost and managerial accounting.
Cost concepts, elements and classification.
Differences among financial, cost and management accounting.

outlineSections.heading: IX. Accounting for Material, Labour and Factory Overheads (FOH)
points: Recognition/valuation principles for material inventory and inventory control methods.
Payroll accounting for labour forms, time rate and piece rate systems, and group incentive schemes.
Factory overhead costs and FOH rate, departmentalization, allocation, apportionment and reapportionment (primary/secondary distributions).
Secondary distribution methods including repeated apportionment/distribution and algebraic method.

outlineSections.heading: X. Costing for Specific Jobs, and Process Costing
points: Nature of a specific job and job-order costing.
Process flow and process costing using cost of production report (CPR).

outlineSections.heading: XI. Management Accounting for Planning, Decision-making and Control
points: Budgeting and its use: meaning/nature of budget and forms including production, sales, cash, flexible, zero-based, and master budget.
Break-even analysis: marginal vs absorption costing, relevant cost concept, use of contribution margin and related concepts in planning/decision-making.
Variance analysis: meaning/use of standards and variances including material, labour and FOH variances and their computation.

outlineSections.heading: I. Fundamental Auditing Principles and Concepts
points: Audit and auditing, true and fair view, audit assertions, reasonable assurance, documentation and audit evidence, audit program, audit risks.
EDP systems and CAAT, inspection, fraud, going concern, audit materiality, misstatement, governance and premise.
Tests of control and substantive procedures.

outlineSections.heading: II. Audit Considerations, Dimensions and Conduct
points: Internal control system and internal audit, internal vs external audit, responsibility for financial statements.
Audit planning, scope and objectives of audit, inherent limitations, risk assessment and management, and corporate governance.
Classification of audit, qualities of auditor, auditing in EDP systems/CAAT.
General auditing principles and techniques for merchandising, manufacturing, banking, insurance, and investment entities.
Audit performance and completion.

outlineSections.heading: III. Role and Responsibilities of an Auditor
points: Professional and legal rights, responsibilities, duties and liabilities of auditor.
Auditor’s opinion and report, and their types.
As specified under Companies Ordinance 1984 and IFAC handbook.

outlineSections.heading: IV. Tax Structure and Fundamental Concepts vis-à-vis Income Tax in Pakistan
points: Tax structure in Pakistan and definitions/terminologies under Section 2 of Income Tax Ordinance 2001.

outlineSections.heading: V. Income Tax and Sales Tax Principles and Application
points: Selected income tax provisions: income for tax purposes, heads of income, tax payable, salary income, property income, business income, capital gains, other sources, tax credits, taxation of individuals/AOPs/companies, due date of payment, and withholding tax.
Related Income Tax Rules 2002.

Selected sales tax provisions: scope, exempt supply, goods, input tax, registered person, supply, tax, retail price/retailer, taxable activity/supply, tax fraction, tax period, time of supply, and determination of tax liability.

outlineSections.heading: VI. Business Studies
points: Nature and scope of business entity and contemporary challenges.
Legal forms: sole proprietorship, partnership, joint stock company, their features, formation and management.
Business combinations and scope, business cycle and implications, role of information technology in business.

outlineSections.heading: VII. Finance
points: Meaning, nature and scope of finance and financial management.
Business finance modes: short-, medium-, and long-term financing.
Nature/scope of financial markets and institutions; features/classification of financial markets.
Financial management techniques: time value of money, cost of capital and capital budgeting techniques.

outlineSections.heading: I. Concept of Integrated Agriculture
points: Components of natural resources as bases for agriculture production (land, water, biological, environmental, solar, energy).

outlineSections.heading: II. Challenges in Pakistan's Agriculture
points: Present scenario and future prospects.
Analytical overview: issues and strategies for improvement of crop management, livestock management, fisheries, cottage industry, resource management and rural development.
Institutions and policies: issues and options.

outlineSections.heading: III. Elements of Climate and their Relationship with Crop Growth
points: Farming systems, biological nitrogen fixation, soil profile, structure and texture, soil fertility, soil erosion and conservation, water logging and salinity.

outlineSections.heading: IV. Genetic Improvement for Crop Production
points: GMO crops and seed production technology.

outlineSections.heading: V. Horticulture
points: Floriculture and landscaping.
Pests and diseases of agriculture crops and their control.
Integrated pest management.

outlineSections.heading: VI. Rainfed and Irrigated Agriculture
points: Agriculture mechanization, land tenure and land reforms, role of agriculture in national economy.

outlineSections.heading: I. Forest, Rangelands and Wildlife Importance and Significance
II. Forest Management and Utilization
points: Wood based industries in Pakistan and silviculture.

outlineSections.heading: IV. National and International Forest Wealth Statistics
V. Role of Wildlife as Value Addition to Forestry
VI. Forest Based Wildlife Resources of Pakistan and their Management
points: Eco-tourism.

outlineSections.heading: VII. Forestry, Agroforestry, Social Forestry and Forest Biometrics
VIII. Socio-economic and Ecological Impact of Man-made Forests
IX. Watershed Management and Role of Forests in Prevailing Climate Change Dilemma
X. National Forest Laws and Policies at National Level
points: Biodiversity and environment.

outlineSections.heading: I. Anthropology
points: Definition of anthropology, its historical development and recent trends.

outlineSections.heading: II. Social Anthropology
points: Definition of culture, its characteristics and functions.
Relationship of anthropology with other social sciences.
Sub-fields of anthropology: biological anthropology, archaeology, linguistic anthropology, socio-cultural anthropology.
Institution of family and marriage: definitions, types, structures, functions, family organization.
Kinship and social organization: definitions, types, functions, kinship terminology.
Economic organization: definitions, evolution, substantivism vs formalism, reciprocity, production, consumption, distribution, barter and primitive economic systems.

Political organization: definitions, evolution of political system, characteristics of band/tribal/chiefdom/state societies; theories of origin of state societies (internal conflict, external conflict, population and irrigation, institutionalization of leadership and emergence of state, system theories); origin of civilization; politics of identity; ethnicity and ethnic relations; nationalism, modernism, post-modernism.
Religion: definitions, evolution of primitive religions, functions of religion, comparison of divine religions and other world religions such as Hinduism, Buddhism, Jainism.
Contemporary human problems: poverty, social inequality, political instability, population problems, ethnic violence and terrorism.

outlineSections.heading: III. Urban Anthropology
points: Rural-urban migration, expansion of cities, major environmental issues, sanitation problems.
Urbanization and development, slums and squatter settlements, refugees, yankees, betties, gypsies, wars and conflict.
Conversion of power from feudal to industrialists, institutionalization, education system, and change in mode of production (agriculture to capitalists).
Poverty (theories and remedies).
Management of city life: psychological, cultural, economic, political, religious, physical, environmental, ecological, demographical, lingual aspects.
Karl Marx and conflict theory.
Problems created by mechanization and automation.

outlineSections.heading: IV. Socio-Cultural Change
points: Definitions and difference between social and cultural change.
Dimensions of cultural change and barriers to change (cultural, psychological, political).
Internal and external dynamics for change.
Population increase and change, diffusion of innovations.
Socio-religious barriers in accepting innovations and new ideas.
Media and cultural change.
Dynamics of change in Pakistan (trends and prospects).

outlineSections.heading: V. Ethnicity and Race
points: Theories related to ethnicity and race, ethnicity and racism, nations and nationality, ethnic conflict, degree of social variation, rank societies, caste and class societies, social stratification.

outlineSections.heading: VI. Anthropological Theories
points: Contributors: Edward Burnett Tylor, Lewis Henry Morgan, James Frazer, Karl Marx, Edmund Leach, Franz Boas, Margaret Mead, Ruth Benedict, Alfred L. Kroeber, Alfred Reginald Radcliffe-Brown, Bronislaw Kasper Malinowski, Clifford Geertz, Talal Asad, Akbar S. Ahmad, Ibn Khaldun, Shah Waliullah.
Classical theories: degeneration, evolutionism, neo-evolutionism, diffusion.
Modern theories: functionalism, structural-functionalism, class struggle, structuralism, historical particularism, feminism, culture and personality.
Current trends in anthropological thought: post-modernism, romanticism, poetics and politics of ethnography.

outlineSections.heading: VII. Anthropological Research Methods
points: Meaning, definition, types and aims of anthropological research.
Qualitative and quantitative research.
Purpose of research, research question, variables, hypothesis, research objectives, research design, sampling.
Field data collection and tools of data collection (questionnaire, interview, participant observation).
Data classification, data analysis and reporting.

outlineSections.heading: I. Vector Calculus (10%)
points: Vector algebra; scalar and vector products of vectors.
Gradient, divergence and curl of a vector.
Line, surface and volume integrals.
Green's, Stokes' and Gauss theorems.

outlineSections.heading: II. Statics (10%)
points: Composition and resolution of forces; parallel forces and couples.
Equilibrium of a system of coplanar forces.
Centre of mass of a system of particles and rigid bodies.
Equilibrium of forces in three dimensions.

outlineSections.heading: III. Dynamics (10%)
points: Motion in a straight line with constant and variable acceleration; simple harmonic motion; conservative forces and principles of energy.
Tangential, normal, radial and transverse components of velocity and acceleration.
Motion under central forces, planetary orbits and Kepler laws.

outlineSections.heading: IV. Ordinary Differential Equations (20%)
points: First-order equations: separable, exact and first-order linear equations; orthogonal trajectories; nonlinear equations reducible to linear form; Bernoulli and Riccati equations.
Equations with constant coefficients; homogeneous and inhomogeneous equations; Cauchy-Euler equations; variation of parameters.
Ordinary and singular points of a differential equation; series solutions; Bessel and Legendre equations; properties of Bessel functions and Legendre polynomials.

outlineSections.heading: V. Fourier Series and Partial Differential Equations (20%)
points: Trigonometric Fourier series; sine and cosine series; Bessel inequality; summation of infinite series; convergence of Fourier series.
First-order partial differential equations; classification of second-order PDEs.
Boundary value problems and solution by separation of variables.
Problems associated with Laplace equation, wave equation and heat equation in Cartesian coordinates.

outlineSections.heading: VI. Numerical Methods (30%)
points: Solution of nonlinear equations by bisection, secant and Newton-Raphson methods; fixed-point iterative method; order of convergence.
Solution of linear systems; diagonally dominant systems; Jacobi and Gauss-Seidel methods.
Numerical differentiation and integration: trapezoidal rule, Simpson's rules, Gaussian integration formulas.
Numerical solution of ordinary differential equations: Euler and modified Euler methods; Runge-Kutta methods.

outlineSections.heading: A. Pre-Islamic Period (العصر الجاھلي)
points: Influence of poets and poetry in Jahiliia period. (أثر الشعر و الشعرآء في العصر الجاھلي)
Literary markets in pre-Islamic Arabs especially Ukkaz. (أسواق الأدب في العصر الجاھلي خاصة سوق عكاظ)
Purposes and features of pre-Islamic poetry with special reference to Mu'allaqat. (أغراض الشعر الجاھلي و مزایاه مع التركیز على المعلقات)

outlineSections.heading: B. Dawn of Islam (عصر صدر الإسلام)
points: Eloquence and rhetoric of Holy Quran with examples from Quranic verses. (فصاحة القرآن و بلاغتھ مع الأمثلة من القرآن الكریم)
Impact of Quran and Hadith on subsequent literature. (أثر القرآن و الحدیث في الأدب العربي)
Poetry at the dawn of Islam. (الشعر في عصر صدر الإسلام)

outlineSections.heading: C. Umayyad Period (العصر الأموي)
points: Art of Flyting. (فن النقائض)
Ghazal platonic and erotic. (الغزل الصریح والغزل العذري)

outlineSections.heading: D. Abbasid and Spanish Period (العصر العباسی والأندلسي)
points: Purposes and features of Abbasid poetry with special emphasis on the poetry of Mutanabbi, Abu Tammam, Abu Nuwas, Abul Atahia. (أغراض الشعر العباسي و میزاتھ مع التركیز على شعر المتنبي و أبي تمام و أبي نواس وأبي العتاھیة)

Prose and its different styles with special emphasis on style of Ibnul Ameed, Ibnul Muqaffa, Al-Jahiz and Al-Qazi al Fazil. (النثر و أسالیبھ المختلفة خاصة أسلوب ابن العمید و ابن المقفع والجاحظ و القاضي الفاضل)
Spanish poetry with special reference to poetry of Ibn e Zaidoon. (الشعر الأندلسي خاصة شعر ابن زیدون)

outlineSections.heading: E. Contemporary Arabic Literature (الأدب العربي المعاصر)
points: Development of drama with special focus on services of Toufeeq al Hakeem. (تطور المسرحیة مع التركیز على أعمال توفیق الحكیم)
Development of novel with special reference to the novels of Taha Husain and Nageeb Mahfooz. (تطور الروایة مع التركیز على روایات طھ حسین و نجیب محفوظ)
Development of short story with special focus on short stories of Mahmood Taimoor. (تطور القصة القصیرة مع نموذج من القصص القصیرة عند محمود تیمور)
Poetry with special focus on poetry of Ahmad Shouqi and Hafiz Ibraheem. (خصائص الشعر مع التركیز على شعر أحمد شوقي و حافظ إبراھیم)

outlineSections.heading: F. Common Topics of Different Periods
points: Criticism from pre-Islamic era to the 4th Islamic century. (النقد في الأدب العربي: من العصر الجاھلي إلى القرن الرابع الھجري)
Art of oratory from pre-Islamic era to Umayyad period. (الخطابة: من العصر الجاھلي إلى العصر الأموي)

Development of Arabic literature in the Sub-Continent: Ghulam Ali Azad in poetry and Shah WaliUllah in prose. (تطور الأدب العربي في شبھ القارة الھندیة: غلام علي آزاد في الشعر و شاه ولي االله في النثر)

outlineSections.heading: H. Arabic Grammar (قواعد العربیة)
points: Syntax (النحو): kinds of sentence (nominal and verbal), kinds of noun (proper/common, masculine/feminine, singular/dual/plural, mu'rab/mabni), case-ending. (أقسام الجملة: الفعلیة و الإسمیة-- أقسام الإسم: "المعرفة و النكرة", "المؤنث و المذكر" "المفرد والتثنیة و الجمع", "المعرب والمبني—الإعراب)

Morphology (الصرف): etymology (roots), mujarrad, mazeed-feeh, transitive and intransitive verb, active and passive voice. (الإشتقاق-- المجرد والمزید فیھ--الفعل اللازم و المتعدي—الفعل المبني المعلوم و المبني المجھول )

outlineSections.heading: I. Algae, Fungi and Bryophytes
points: Phycology: distribution, classification, structure, life history and economic importance of the main groups of algae.

Mycology and plant pathology: structure, reproduction, classification and economic importance of the main groups of fungi; diseases of economically important crops and general principles of their control.
Bryology: structure and reproduction of bryophytes; evolution of gametophyte and sporophyte.

outlineSections.heading: II. Pteridophyta and Gymnosperms
points: General account with special reference to structure, life history and affinities of both pteridophytes and gymnosperms.
Ontogeny and structure of seed, classification and economic importance of gymnosperms.

outlineSections.heading: III. Anatomy and Embryology
points: Primary and secondary tissues, meristems, secondary growth in dicot stem, anatomy of leaf, stem and root.
Micro and megasporogenesis, pollination mechanism, fertilization, development of embryo and endosperm, seed dispersal.

outlineSections.heading: IV. Taxonomy of Angiosperms
points: Systems of classification and rules of botanical nomenclature.
Concepts of speciation.
Introduction to modern trends in plant taxonomy: biosystematics, chemotaxonomy and numerical taxonomy.
General characters and economic importance of common angiosperm families.

outlineSections.heading: V. Plant Physiology
points: Plant water relations, osmotic quantities, component potentials of water and role in transport, water absorption by roots, transpiration.
Role of essential mineral elements and their uptake, plant hormones, photoperiodism, vernalization, dormancy, seed germination, enzymes.
Photosynthesis: plant pigments, light reaction, CO2 fixation, mechanism of photophosphorylation.
Respiration: glycolysis, Krebs cycle, mechanism of oxidative phosphorylation.

outlineSections.heading: VI. Ecology
points: Influence of climatic, edaphic and biotic factors on plant growth; vegetation sampling techniques.
Concepts of ecosystems and productivity, ecological energetics, pyramids (numbers, biomass, energy), trophic levels, food chains and food webs.
Biogeochemical cycles (hydrological and nitrogen), succession.
Causes and reclamation of soil salinity and water logging in Pakistan; soil erosion and control; soil conservation methods; deforestation; biodiversity conservation; pollution.

outlineSections.heading: VII. Cytology
points: Cell cycle, cellular morphology, chemistry of cell wall and cell membrane, cell-to-cell communication, plant tissue and cell culture, cell senescence and cell death.
Ultra-structure of organelles: mitochondria, Golgi bodies, endoplasmic reticulum, plastids, ribosomes, glyoxysomes, vacuoles, nucleus.

outlineSections.heading: VIII. Genetics
points: Mendelian genetics, multiple alleles, polygenic inheritance, gene interaction, epistasis and pleiotropy, sex-linked inheritance, chromosomal aberrations, mutations, DNA repair.

outlineSections.heading: IX. Evolution
points: Introduction of evolution, evolutionary history, evolution of life, convergent evolution, divergent evolution, parallel evolution and natural selection.

outlineSections.heading: X. Molecular Biology
points: Nucleic acids, DNA as hereditary material, DNA replication, transcription, genetic code, protein synthesis, genetic engineering and its application, genetically modified organisms (GMO).

outlineSections.heading: I. Management
points: Defining organization, management, and management in organizations.
Four management functions, management roles, management skills.
Organizational internal-external environment.
Management planning, goal setting and decision making.
Strategic management process: strategy formulation and implementation.
Developing organizational structure and design.
Designing adaptive organizations.
Managing change and innovation.
Leadership and motivation.

outlineSections.heading: II. HR Management
points: Role of human resource management in organizational performance.
Functions of HRM.
Process and methods of job analysis.
Planning and forecasting personnel needs.
Recruitment and selection.
Training and development.
Performance management and appraisal: methods and processes.
Establishing strategic pay plans.
Compensation and benefits.
Ethics, justice and fair treatment in HR management.
Labor relations and collective bargaining.

outlineSections.heading: III. Financial Management
points: Overview of financial management.

Introduction/significance of financial markets; real assets vs financial assets; types of financial markets; role of capital and money markets in economic development; organizational goals and shareholder wealth maximization perspective.

Time value of money: cost of money and factors affecting cost, interest rate fundamentals/determinants, future/present value, timelines, annuities, perpetuities, mixed cash flow streams, compounding (discrete/continuous), loan amortization.
Analysis and interpretation of financial statements: horizontal/vertical/common-size/ratio/comparative/index trend analysis, forecasting, and evaluation of credit/management/profitability/risk.

Risk, return and introduction to pricing: expected return, standalone risk (standard deviation/coefficient of variation), risk aversion and required return, portfolio risk (diversifiable vs market), SML and CAPM, WACC, discounting process and relevant risk-return for valuation.
Cash flow and budgeting: significance of budgeting, cash budgets, financial forecasts, profit vs cash flow, reading/analyzing statement of cash flow.
Capital budgeting: significance, incremental cash flows, decision rules (NPV, IRR, MIRR, return), optimal capital structure, discount rate, capital rationing.

outlineSections.heading: IV. Operations and Supply Chain Management
a. Operations Management
points: Operations and productivity: OM as one of three core organizational functions, significance/contributions, future trends, and differences between goods and services.
Operations strategy in global environment: developing mission and OM strategies, critical success factors (CSF), aligning core competencies with CSF.
Process strategy: four process strategies, process analysis/design, process mapping, flow diagrams, process charts, service process design, process re-engineering.
Capacity planning: design/effective capacity, capacity cushion, demand management, leading vs lagging strategies, single and multiple product break-even analysis.
Location strategies: factors affecting decisions, factor rating, load-distance, center of gravity, service location strategy.
Layout strategies: layout types/design, fixed position layout, process-oriented layouts, office layout, retail layout, assembly line balancing.
Inventory management: role of inventory, ABC analysis, record accuracy, cycle counting, inventory models, fixed period and continuous review systems, EOQ, safety stock, service level.

outlineSections.heading: b. Supply Chain Management

Supply chain performance: achieving strategic fit, challenges, cost, quality and lead time.
Supply chain drivers: facilities, inventory, information, transportation, sourcing and pricing.
Balancing supply and demand: bullwhip effect, demand collaboration, information sharing, accurate response strategy.
Supply chain coordination: obstacles, vendor managed inventory, collaborative planning forecasting and replenishment, managerial levers for coordination.
IT in supply chain management: role of IT, customer relationship management, supplier relationship management, IT risk management, supply chain IT in practice.

outlineSections.heading: I. Atomic Structure and Quantum Chemistry
points: Electromagnetic spectrum, photoelectric effect, Bohr's atomic model, wave and particle nature of light matter.
de Broglie's equation, Heisenberg's uncertainty principle, wave functions and Born interpretation of wave functions.
Probability density, Eigen functions and Eigen values, Hamiltonian operator.
Schrodinger wave equation and its solution for particle in one and three dimensional box.

outlineSections.heading: II. Electrochemistry
points: Ions in solution, measurement of conductance and Kohlrausch's law.
Mobility of ions and transport number, conductometric titrations, Debye-Huckel theory and activity coefficient, determination of activities.
Redox reactions, spontaneous reactions, electrochemical cells, standard electrode potentials, liquid junction potential, electrochemical series, Nernst's equation.
Measurement of pH, electrolytic cells, potentiometry, reference and indicator electrodes, fuel cells, corrosion and its prevention.

outlineSections.heading: III. Thermodynamics
points: Equation of states, ideal and real gases, Van der Waals equation for real gases, critical phenomena and critical constants.
Four laws of thermodynamics and their applications, thermochemistry, calorimetry.
Heat capacities and dependence on temperature, pressure and volume; reversible/non-reversible and spontaneous/non-spontaneous processes.
Hess's law, Born-Haber cycle, relations of entropy and Gibbs free energy with equilibrium constant, Gibbs-Helmholtz equation, fugacity and activity.

outlineSections.heading: IV. Chemical Kinetics
points: Rate and molecularity of reactions; factors affecting reaction rate.
Zero, first, second and third order reactions with same initial concentrations; half-lives of reactions.
Experimental techniques for determination of order of reaction: integration, half-life, initial rate and graphical methods.
Collision theory, transition state theory, Arrhenius equation and rate equations of complex reactions.

outlineSections.heading: V. Surface Chemistry and Catalysis
points: Properties of liquids, physical and chemical properties of surface, determination of surface area.
Adsorption and absorption; physical adsorption and chemisorption; Langmuir and Freundlich adsorption isotherms.
Colloids: properties, classification and preparation of colloidal systems; surfactants.
Phase rule and Gibbs phase rule equation; one-component and two-component systems with examples.
Catalysis: homogeneous and heterogeneous catalysis, acid-base and enzyme catalysis.

outlineSections.heading: VI. Fundamentals of Chemometrics
points: Sampling, significant figures, stoichiometric calculations, measurement errors.
Analysis of variance (ANOVA), arithmetic mean, median, mode, standard deviation/relative standard deviation, confidence limits, Gaussian distribution, least square method, statistical tests.

outlineSections.heading: VII. Separation Methods
points: Solvent extraction: theory of solvent extraction, solvent extraction of metals, analytical separations, multiple batch extraction and counter current distribution.
Chromatography: theory of chromatography, classification and overview of paper, thin layer, column and ion exchange chromatographies.
Principle of electrophoresis and its application in separation and characterization of proteins.

outlineSections.heading: VIII. Basic Inorganic Chemistry
points: Types of chemical bonding: ionic and covalent bonding, localized bond approach, theories of chemical bonding.
Valence bond theory (VBT), hybridization and resonance, prediction of molecular shapes using VSEPR model.
Molecular orbital theory (MOT) applied to diatomic molecules, delocalized approach to bonding, bonding in electron deficient compounds, hydrogen bonding.
Physical and chemical properties of p-block elements with emphasis on oxygen, carbon, chlorine, silicon, nitrogen, phosphorus and representative compounds.

outlineSections.heading: IX. Acids and Bases
points: Brief concepts of chemical equilibrium, acid-base theories including soft and hard acid-base (SHAB) concept.
Relative strength of acids and bases; significance of pH, pKa, pKb and buffer solutions.
Theory of indicators, solubility, solubility product, common ion effect and their industrial applications.

outlineSections.heading: X. Chemistry of d and f-block elements
points: General characteristics of d-block elements and background of coordination chemistry.
Nomenclature and structure of coordination complexes with coordination number 2-10; chelates and chelate effect.
Theories of coordination complexes: Werner's theory, VBT, CFT and MOT; Jahn-Teller theorem.
Magnetic properties, spectral properties, isomerism, stereochemistry and stability constants of coordination complexes.
Lanthanides: occurrence, extraction, separation principles, electronic structure, periodic position, lanthanide contraction, oxidation states, spectral/magnetic properties and uses.
Actinides: electronic structure, oxidation states, periodic position, half-life and decay law.

outlineSections.heading: I. Basic Concepts of Organic Chemistry
points: Bonding and orbital hybridization, localized and delocalized bonding.
Inductive effect, dipole moment, resonance, hyperconjugation.

outlineSections.heading: II. Saturated and Unsaturated Hydrocarbon
points: Nomenclature, physical properties, preparation and reactions of alkanes, alkenes and alkynes.

outlineSections.heading: III. Chemistry of Aromatic Compounds
points: Benzene structure, aromaticity, mechanism of electrophilic substitution reaction.
Activating and deactivating substituents; effects on orientation and reactivity.

outlineSections.heading: IV. Chemistry of Functional Groups
points: Preparation and properties of alcohols, phenols, ethers and amines with reaction mechanisms and applications.
Preparation and reactions of alkyl halides; synthetic applications of Grignard reagent.
Carbonyl compounds: preparation and reaction mechanism of aldehydes and ketones and their applications.
Carboxylic acids and derivatives: acidity and substituent effects; preparation and reactions of acid halides, acid anhydrides, esters and amides.

outlineSections.heading: V. Aliphatic Nucleophilic Substitution and Elimination Reactions
points: Mechanism of nucleophilic substitution reactions.
Elimination reactions, Zaitsev rule and Hofmann rule.
Competition between substitution and elimination reactions.

outlineSections.heading: VI. Stereochemistry
points: Molecular chirality and types of stereoisomers.
R,S configuration and E,Z designation.
Optical activity, stereoselectivity and stereospecificity.
Resolution of racemic mixtures.

outlineSections.heading: VII. Organic Spectroscopy
points: Theory, principle, instrumentation and applications of UV/Visible, 1H NMR, IR and mass spectroscopic techniques.

outlineSections.heading: VIII. Biomolecules
points: Carbohydrates: monosaccharides, oligosaccharides and polysaccharides; biological functions of starch, glycogen, cellulose and cell wall polysaccharides.
Lipids: classification and biological importance; significance in biological membranes and transport mechanism.
Amino acids: classification, physical and chemical properties, biological significance.
Proteins: classification, properties and biological significance; primary, secondary, tertiary and quaternary structures.
Nucleic acids: chemical composition, structure and biological significance.
Enzymes: enzyme-substrate interactions, active site, mechanism of action, single-substrate kinetics, inhibition, regulatory and allosteric enzymes.

outlineSections.heading: IX. Metabolism
points: Digestion, absorption and transport of proteins, carbohydrates, lipids and nucleic acids.
Glycolysis, citric acid cycle, gluconeogenesis, glycogenesis, glycogenolysis and photosynthesis.
Biosynthesis of triglycerides, phosphides, steroids, bile acids and ketone bodies.
Biochemical reactions of amino acids: decarboxylation, deamination, transamination, transmethylation, urea cycle, creatine and uric acid synthesis.
Catabolism of nucleosides, DNA polymerases and other enzymes involved in metabolism.

outlineSections.heading: X. Chemical Industries
points: Manufacturing and processing of sugar, cement, glass, paper, fertilizers, soap and detergents.

outlineSections.heading: I. Introduction to Computing

Computer system components and communication system, input/output devices and types, storage media and types.

User interfaces, major software issues, creation/formatting/maintenance of computer documents.

Computers and society, information security/privacy, computer crimes and ethical challenges, viruses, plagiarism, intellectual property rights.

outlineSections.heading: II. Programming Fundamentals

Components of a programming language, program development and execution, program structure.
Data types and variable declarations, standard I/O streams and statements, control structures.
Standard library functions, user-defined functions and parameter passing.
Arrays, pointers, strings, structures, unions, and bit manipulation operators.

outlineSections.heading: III. Object Oriented Paradigm

Classes and objects: data members and member functions.
Advanced classes: friends, static, composition, this, const.
Operator overloading: stream insertion/extraction, binary and unary operators.
Inheritance: single, multiple, protected members, method overriding.
Polymorphism: virtual functions, pure virtual functions, abstract class and abstract super class.
Standard Template Library (STL), files and streams (sequential and random access), file processing, exception handling.

outlineSections.heading: IV. Algorithms & Data Structures
points: Fundamental concepts, properties and criteria of algorithms.
Algorithm representations, pseudo code and flow charts, designing algorithms, algorithm analysis and asymptotic notations.
Classification of lists, abstract data types, implementation of stacks and queues using ADTs.
Searching and sorting: linear search, binary search, bubble sort, merge sort, quick sort, heap sort.
Stacks, queues, hash tables (linear probing, bucketing, chaining), recursion.
Trees (binary trees, binary search trees, AVL trees, two-three trees), graphs, heuristic search, genetic algorithms.
Encryption algorithms (DES, RSA).

outlineSections.heading: V. Software Engineering
points: Software processes, process models, agile software development.
Analysis modeling, requirements engineering, design concepts, architectural design, design and implementation.
Software testing, system delivery and maintenance, software evolution, formal specification.
Software quality assurance, introduction to proofs of correctness.
Distributed software engineering, aspect-oriented software engineering, project management, process improvement.

outlineSections.heading: VI. Compiler Construction

Lexical analysis: input buffering, token specification/recognition, regular expressions, finite automata.

Syntax directed translation: synthesized and inherited attributes, syntax tree construction, top-down translation.
Semantic analysis: symbol tables, type expressions, type checking.
Intermediate code generation and code generation.
Code optimization: redundant code elimination, constant folding, loop and peephole optimization, optimization issues.

points: Fundamental concepts, overview of computer systems, evolution and performance, architectural levels, virtual machines.
Processor types, metrics, machine instructions, instruction execution cycle, CISC vs RISC, parallelism.
Internal/external data representation, interconnections, cache memory, internal/external memory, I/O systems.
Microprocessor and bus structure, I/O types, bus types, memory organization and structure.
Instruction representation, characteristics and processing, processor structure and function.
Control unit operation, microprogrammed control, instruction-level parallelism and superscalar processors.
Parallel processing, multi-processor and multi-core systems.

Layering: OSI and TCP/IP.

Transport layer: UDP/TCP multiplexing, connectionless transport, reliable data transfer, congestion control.

Memory management and virtual memory management.
File systems (UNIX and Windows), I/O management.

Functional dependencies and normalization, storage and indexing structures.
XML documents and web services, query processing/evaluation/optimization.

Database security and access control.

Image transformations: translation, scaling, rotation, shear.
Image histogram and enhancement: contrast, smoothing, sharpening.
Gray-scale and color images; color models (RGB, CMYK, HIS).
Image restoration and noise models.
Morphological operators: erosion, dilation, opening, closing, skeletonization, thinning.
Image segmentation, point/line/edge/boundary detection, image compression.

HTML, software architecture styles/patterns/frameworks, components/classification of web architecture.
Layered architectures: client-server, n-layered, JSP model, struts, OOHDM; integration/data aspect architectures.
CSS properties, JavaScript functionalities/events/variables/operators, DOM, XML, RSS, API.
Client-side programming with HTML/XHTML/XML/JavaScript/CSS and server-side programming with PHP.
Web development process, methodologies, promotion and deployment.
Web application issues: accessibility, testing, performance, operation, maintenance, security.

outlineSections.heading: II. Reading Comprehension (20 marks)

points: Definition and scope, psychology as a science, schools, perspectives, models of psychology, recent trends.

outlineSections.heading: II. Biological Basis of Behaviour
points: Nervous system, neuron and its function, central and peripheral nervous system, endocrine system.

outlineSections.heading: III. Sensation and Perception
points: Sensory process, perception, Gestalt principles, binocular and monocular cues, illusions and extra sensory perception, determinants of perception.

outlineSections.heading: IV. Learning and Memory
points: Nature and forms of learning.
Classical and operant conditioning, reinforcement, extinction, discrimination, punishment, observational learning.
Theories of learning.
Types/process/theories of memory and forgetting.

outlineSections.heading: V. Motivation and Emotion
points: Homeostasis, factors affecting motivation, biogenic and social motives, measurement of human motivation, theories of motivation.
Emotions, types of emotions, physiological changes in emotion, theories of emotions.

outlineSections.heading: VI. Psychological Assessment
points: Attributes of psychological measures, validity, reliability, item analysis, norms, modern test theory.
Selection and training, educational and clinical assessment, ethical and legal issues in assessment.

outlineSections.heading: VII. Personality
points: Determinants and developmental factors of personality, theoretical perspectives, personality assessment and techniques, cross-cultural issues.

outlineSections.heading: VIII. Intelligence
points: Theories of intelligence, types of intelligence (IQ, EQ), assessing intelligence.

outlineSections.heading: IX. Social Influence and Group Dynamics
points: Social facilitation, attribution, conformity, obedience, altruism, attitudes, social norms.

outlineSections.heading: X. Developmental Psychology
points: Physical, cognitive, social and emotional development in childhood, adolescence, adulthood and old age.

outlineSections.heading: XI. Abnormal and Clinical Psychology
points: Concept and causes of abnormality, clinical assessment and intervention.
Disorders such as schizophrenia, mood disorder, anxiety disorder, personality disorder.
Psychological treatment including therapeutic interventions.

outlineSections.heading: XII. Organizational/Industrial Psychology
points: Leadership styles, decision making, work motivation, organizational culture.
Stress and conflict at work and management, organizational socialization, job-related attitude.
Sexual harassment, glass ceiling, human-computer interaction.

outlineSections.heading: XIII. Health Psychology
points: Beliefs and behavior, models of health psychology, assessment and intervention, models of stress, chronic and terminal illness, role of social support.

outlineSections.heading: XIV. Forensic Psychology
points: Psychology and law, investigation, confession, eyewitness testimony, working with offenders, juvenile delinquents, drug addicts, sex offenders.

outlineSections.heading: I. Public Administration: Concepts, Approaches and Context
points: Definitions; role and scope of public administration in society.
Issues in public administration theory and practice: democracy vs bureaucracy, politics vs administration, efficiency vs equity.
Core values of public administration: rule of law, efficiency, equity and fairness, responsiveness.
Traditional public administration, new public management, new public service, governance approach to public administration.
Islamic concept of public administration and historical roots of public administration in Pakistan.

outlineSections.heading: II. Public Administration: Classical and Contemporary Theories and Concepts
points: Bureaucracy, scientific management, human relations approach.
Leadership, motivation, network governance, strategic management, public choice theory.
Types of organizational structure.
Organization of federal, provincial and local government in Pakistan.
Administrative culture of Pakistan and inter-governmental relations at federal and provincial level.

outlineSections.heading: III. Public Policy Planning, Implementation and Evaluation
points: Strategic planning and management, planning process, policy analysis, policy implementation and program evaluation.
Planning machinery.
Role of donors and international institutions in public policy and management.
Policy making and implementation in Pakistan.

outlineSections.heading: IV. Budgeting and Financial Management
points: Budget as a policy tool and managerial tool.
Principles of budgeting, audit and accounting in government.
Line-item budgeting, performance budgeting, program budgeting, zero-base budgeting, outcome-based budgeting.
Planning and budgeting in Pakistan.

outlineSections.heading: V. Managing Human Resources
points: Spoil system vs merit system in public employment.
Personnel vs human resources management.
Close system vs open system of public employment.
Functions of human resources management.
Implementation of HRM in public sector: key issues and challenges.

outlineSections.heading: VI. Administrative Law
points: Meaning, scope and significance.
Nature and contents of administrative law, administrative ethics, delegation of authority and legislation, administrative tribunals.
Administrative law in Pakistan.

outlineSections.heading: VII. Public Management Skills
points: Planning, decision making, conflict management, leading, communication, administrative buffering.
Managing change, managing diversity, stress management, delegation.
Public service motivation, creativity and problem solving.
Issues of public management.

outlineSections.heading: VIII. The Civil Service of Pakistan
points: Historical background and structure of civil service.
History of civil service reform and management of civil service.
Institutional and cultural context of civil service.
Role of civil service in good governance, gender and civil service.

outlineSections.heading: IX. Organization of Provincial and Local Government
points: Governance structure of provincial administration and organization of provincial secretariat.
Organization/functions of provincial authorities and agencies and relationship with government departments.
Post-devolution local governance.
Organization/functions of district government and administration.
Organization and structure of city district government.
Issues and challenges of local governance.

outlineSections.heading: X. Governance and Administrative Reforms
points: Theories and types of administrative reforms.
Privatization, regulation, de-regulation, decentralization, partnerships and collaboration.
Business re-engineering and quality assurance.
Administrative reform in Pakistan.

outlineSections.heading: XI. Public Administration Accountability & Control
points: Bureaucratic responsiveness, representative bureaucracy, and citizens engagement in public service.
Accountability and control; concept and approaches to public accountability.
Institutional framework for administrative accountability.
Legislative, executive and judicial control over administration.
Administrative corruption; role of civil society in good governance; media, interest groups and civil society organizations.
Situation in Pakistan.

outlineSections.heading: XII. Public Administration and Development
points: Role of public administration in development.
Concept of development administration.
Difference between development administration and development management.
Changing role of public administration in development.
Issues and challenges of public administration in Pakistan.

outlineSections.heading: I. Modern Algebra
points: Group, subgroups, Lagrange's theorem, cyclic groups, normal subgroups, quotient groups.
Fundamental theorem of homomorphism; isomorphism theorems of groups; inner automorphisms; conjugate elements and conjugate subgroups; commutator subgroups.
Ring, subrings, integral domains, quotient fields, isomorphism theorems, field extension and finite fields.

Vector spaces, linear independence, bases, dimension of finitely generated spaces; linear transformations; matrices and matrix algebra; reduction to echelon form; rank and nullity of a linear transformation.
Solution of homogeneous and non-homogeneous linear equation systems; properties of determinants.

outlineSections.heading: II. Calculus & Analytic Geometry
points: Real numbers, limits, continuity, differentiability, indefinite integration, mean value theorems, Taylor's theorem, indeterminate forms, asymptotes and curve tracing.
Definite integrals, functions of several variables, partial derivatives, maxima/minima, Jacobians, double and triple integration (techniques only).
Applications of Beta and Gamma functions, areas and volumes, Riemann-Stieltjes integral, improper integrals and their conditions of existence, implicit function theorem.
Conic sections in Cartesian coordinates; plane polar coordinates and their use for straight lines and conic sections.
Cartesian and spherical polar coordinates in three dimensions; the plane, sphere, ellipsoid, paraboloid and hyperboloid in Cartesian and spherical polar coordinates.

outlineSections.heading: III. Complex Variables
points: Function of a complex variable; De Moivre's theorem and its applications.
Analytic functions, Cauchy's theorem, Cauchy's integral formula, Taylor and Laurent series.
Singularities, Cauchy residue theorem and contour integration.
Fourier series and Fourier transforms.

outlineSections.heading: I. General Sociology
points: Individual: sociability or the sociality of man.

Culture: meaning and characteristics (variable, learnt, social, shared, transmissive, dynamic and adaptive), types (material and non-material), functions (transfer of knowledge, defining situations, behavior patterns, personality molding), and elements (norms, values, beliefs, sanctions, customs). Culture and socialization (formal/non-formal), transmission of culture, cultural relativism, sub-cultures, ethnocentrism and xenocentrism, cultural lag, high culture and popular culture, multiculturalism, assimilation and acculturation.

Society and community: meaning and characteristics; individual and society; relationship between individual and society; social contract theory and organismic theory; social and cultural evolution (hunting and gathering, herding/advanced herding, horticultural, agrarian, industrial and postmodern society).
Social interaction: caste and classes, forms of social classes, feudal system in Pakistan, social mobility and its determinants in Pakistani society, culture of poverty.
Social control: formal and informal mechanisms, anomie, alienation and social integration; means of social integration in Pakistani society.

Social and cultural change and social policy: discovery and processes of change, inhibitions to change in Pakistan, social planning and directed change, effects of industrialization, urbanization, modernization and modern means of communication.
Public opinion: formation of public opinion, concept and characteristics of opinion leadership.
Community: rural community and characteristics of rural life; urban community, rural-urban convergence, urbanism, future of cities in Pakistan.
Social institutions: nature and genesis, institutionalization process, functions of family, religion, education, economy and politics.

Social problems in Pakistan: high population growth, rural-urban migration, technical/vocational training issues, deviance and street crime, unemployment, illiteracy and school dropout, smuggling, prostitution, poverty, drug addiction, child labour and abuse, bonded labour, customs/traditions affecting women, violence against women and domestic violence, issues concerning the elderly.

outlineSections.heading: II. Sociological Theory
points: Three sociological perspectives: structural functionalism, symbolic interactionism and conflict perspective.
Theorists: Ibn-i-Khaldun, Spencer, Auguste Comte, Emile Durkheim, Max Weber, Karl Marx, Parsons.

outlineSections.heading: III. Methods of Sociological Research
points: Scientific method and steps in research.
Types of questionnaire research design, surveys, observation and case studies.

outlineSections.heading: I. Descriptive Statistics
points: Definition, importance and scope of statistics; descriptive and inferential statistics.
Presentation of data: tables, graphs and charts including stem-and-leaf diagram and box-and-whisker plots.
Measures of central tendency/location and measures of dispersion/variability.
Measures of skewness and kurtosis.

outlineSections.heading: II. Basic Probability
points: Basic probability concepts; additive and multiplicative laws of probability.
Joint and marginal probabilities, conditional probability and statistical independence, Bayes' rule.
Random variable, mathematical expectation, discrete and continuous random variables.
Probability distribution, mean and variance of a discrete probability distribution.

outlineSections.heading: III. Probability Distributions
points: Discrete and continuous probability distributions.
Properties and applications of Binomial, Poisson and Hyper-geometric distributions.
Normal distribution and its properties, standard normal curve.
Normal approximation to Binomial and Poisson distribution.

outlineSections.heading: IV. Regression Analysis & Correlation Analysis
points: Concepts of regression and correlation and their applications.
Simple and multiple linear regression (up to three variables).
Estimation of simple regression model parameters, method of least squares, and inference regarding regression parameters.
Correlation coefficient and its properties; inference regarding correlation coefficient.
Partial correlation and multiple correlation coefficients (up to three variables).

outlineSections.heading: V. Non-Parametric Methods
points: Parametric versus non-parametric tests and when to use non-parametric procedures.
One-sample tests: sign test, Wilcoxon signed-ranks test, Kolmogorov-Smirnov test, run test.
Tests for two related samples: sign test, run test, chi-square test.
Tests for two independent samples: Mann-Whitney test, Kolmogorov-Smirnov test.

outlineSections.heading: I. Sampling & Sampling Distributions
points: Population and sample, advantages of sampling, sampling design, probability and non-probability sampling techniques.
Brief concepts of simple random, stratified, systematic, cluster, multiphase and multistage sampling.
Non-probability sampling: purposive, quota, convenience and accidental sampling.
Sampling with and without replacement; application of central limit theorem in sampling.
Sampling distribution of mean, difference between two means, proportion, difference between two proportions, and variance.

outlineSections.heading: II. Statistical Inferences
points: Estimation: point estimation, properties of a good estimator, interval estimation.
Interval estimation of single population mean and single proportion; difference between two means and two proportions.
Hypothesis testing and types of errors; testing for population mean and difference between two population means.
Inference for means of two normal populations using independent samples (equal variances assumed) and paired samples.
Hypothesis testing for single population proportion and difference between two population proportions; sample size estimation.
Analysis of categorized data, goodness-of-fit tests, contingency tables and test of independence.

outlineSections.heading: III. Design of Experiments
points: One-way and two-way analysis of variance; design of experiments.
Concepts of treatment, replication, blocking, experimental units and experimental error.
Basic principles of design of experiments.
Description, layout and statistical analysis of CRD and RCBD.
Multiple comparison tests (LSD test).

outlineSections.heading: IV. Population Analysis & Vital Statistics
points: Population and demographic methods; sources of demographic data.
Basic demographic measures: sex ratio, child women ratio, vital index, crude/specific birth and death rates, total fertility and net reproduction rates.
Official statistics: statistical systems in Pakistan, functions of Statistics Division, Bureaus of Statistics and NADRA.
National income, gross domestic product, saving and wealth, index numbers.

outlineSections.heading: I. Animal Diversity-Invertebrates
points: Architectural pattern of an animal, taxonomy and phylogeny, major subdivisions of animal kingdom.
Animal-like protists (Protozoa): evolutionary perspective, locomotion and reproduction, protozoa of veterinary and medical importance.
Porifera: body wall, skeleton and water current system.
Coelenterates: reproduction plan and alternation of generation (polymorphism), coral reefs.
Platyhelminthes and nematodes: parasitic adaptations and medical importance; annelids: metamerism and ecological importance.
Molluscs: modification of foot, feeding and role in shell fishery.
Arthropods: modification of mouth parts, role as vectors in transmission of microbial infection, ecological importance.
Echinoderms: characteristics, evolutionary perspective, relationships to other animals.

outlineSections.heading: II. Animal Diversity-Chordata
points: Hemichordates and invertebrate chordates: evolutionary perspective and phylogenetic relationships.
Fishes: structural and functional adaptations.
Amphibians: movement onto land and early evolution of terrestrial vertebrates.
Reptiles: characteristics and adaptations in reptilians.
Birds: migration, navigation and adaptations.
Mammals: structural and functional adaptations.

outlineSections.heading: III. Principles of Animal Life
points: Chemical basis of animal life: biomolecules (carbohydrates, lipids, proteins and nucleic acids).
Cell concept/theory; organization of organelles (structure and functions); central dogma (transcription and translation); meiosis and mitosis.
Protozoa: reproduction patterns and parasitism.
Mesozoa and Parazoa; Porifera cell types/body wall/skeleton/water current system; Coelenterata reproduction plan and alternation of generation (polymorphism).
Tissue types: epithelial, connective, muscle and nervous tissues; organs and organ systems.
Enzyme function and factors affecting activity, cofactors and coenzymes; aerobic and anaerobic respiration as major ATP source.
Mendel's laws, chromosomal basis of inheritance, multiple alleles, eukaryotic chromosomes, mutations and chromosomal aberrations.

Ecological concepts: interactions, ecosystem components, food chain/web, biogeochemical cycles, forests, biomes, wildlife conservation/management, environmental pollution, greenhouse effect, acid rain, global warming and climate change.
Evolution: Darwinian theory and evidence; microevolution (variation within species); macroevolution and speciation (allopatric, parapatric, sympatric).

outlineSections.heading: IV. Animal Form and Function
points: Protection, support and movement: integumentary system of invertebrates and vertebrates; muscular systems of invertebrates and vertebrates.
Digestion and nutrition: feeding mechanisms, digestion, organization/regional function of alimentary canal, regulation of food intake, nutritional requirements.
Internal fluids and respiration: internal fluid environment, composition of blood, circulation and respiration mechanisms.
Homeostasis: excretion, vertebrate kidney mechanisms, temperature regulation.
Nervous coordination: nervous system and senses, functional units of nervous system, synaptic junctions between nerves.

Chemical coordination: endocrine system, vertebrate endocrine glands and hormone types, mechanism of hormone action; animal behavior including learning, habituation, insight learning, latent learning, classical learning, control of behavior and social behavior.
